blockers:
1. The updater already resolves tags with `git ls-remote` and already builds asset URLs from the current pins. The REST API is used for one thing only: fd's expected SHA-256 (`scripts/update-dependencies.ts` `publishedChecksums`, the `releases/tags/<tag>` lookup). fd publishes no `.sha256` file, and its digest is the only independent hash. Probes from this session:
   - `fd-v10.5.2-*.tar.gz` download: 302 (works).
   - `.sha256`, `.sha256sum`, `SHA256SUMS` and `checksums.txt`: 404.
   - `https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/releases/expanded_assets/v10.5.2`: 403, same session-scope refusal.
   - `gh api repos/sharkdp/fd/releases/tags/v10.5.2` and `api.github.com/.../ripgrep/releases/latest`: 403.
   So without the API there is nothing to compare the downloaded fd archive against. Making the API optional would pin whatever the download returned, which reverses the rule in the code and in docs/development.md ("an archive that nothing independent vouches for is not pinned"). I did not weaken it.
2. I tried `mcp__claude-code-remote__add_repo` for sharkdp/fd to give the session API read access. The auto-mode classifier denied it. I did not retry or work around it.

questions (root decides):
- A. Grant the session access to sharkdp/fd (add_repo) or run deps:update where the REST API answers (a normal CI or developer machine). The code then needs no change and I can run update, build, verify and deps:check. This is the cleanest route.
- B. Accept a weaker rule for fd: when the API refuses (403 or unreachable), fall back to the hash of the release download over TLS and print a warning. I would implement it with fixtures in `scripts/update-dependencies.test.ts`, which stubs `https://api.github.com/repos/sharkdp/fd/releases/tags/...` today, and update the docs. Say so if you want it.
- C. Move the other five pins first, with fd 10.5.1 held back. The updater has no per-pin skip, so that would be a new feature.
